title: async-evict-heartbeat-drift-remediation
creator: Maya Chen
description: A set of customer escalations across Hosted and Dedicated clusters produced intermittent GPU OOMs and steadily increasing memory fragmentation over multi-hour windows. The fault pattern did not match previous KV handle leaks: OOMs correlated with long GC/eviction pauses on nodes experiencing control-plane heartbeat lag, causing stale GPU allocation maps and orphaned slab reservations that survived session teardown.
impact_summary: Three paying customers on Hosted and two Dedicated customers observed degraded request success rates and elevated tail latencies between 2026-02-18 and 2026-02-20. Customers reported increased error rates and evidence of silent memory retention leading to full-device OOMs. On Dedicated nodes this caused customer-facing throughput drops and manual node restarts.
timeline: 2026-02-18 03:12 UTC - First alert: hosted/gpu-cluster-7 reported 5x baseline OOMs; SRE paged runtime oncall.
2026-02-18 04:00 UTC - Correlated incidents across Hosted and a Dedicated customer; began collecting allocation traces and kv-evict queue metrics.
2026-02-19 09:20 UTC - Reproduced allocation map drift in dev by delaying eviction heartbeat (simulated network stalls); observed orphaned GPU slab allocations not reclaimed after session close.
2026-02-20 13:45 UTC - Proposed runtime patch (epoched allocation toggles + immediate compaction hook) and opened hotfix PR.
2026-02-24 17:10 UTC - PR #2419 merged to canary; canary metrics showed 92% reduction in orphaned allocations and stable tail memory usage.
2026-03-05 11:00 UTC - Running across 10% of Hosted and two Dedicated pools as part of In Review rollout; monitoring indicates resolved for observed customers.
root_cause: The eviction subsystem and GPU allocator used independent liveness signals. When control-plane heartbeats were delayed (network jitter / control plane GC), eviction timers drifted and eviction work queued up. Under queue backlog, eviction processing raced with session teardown: allocator bitmap updates were applied out-of-order leading to transiently detached slab references. Those detached slabs were not reachable by the live allocator path and therefore not reclaimed until a full compaction run, which did not run under heavy pressure, causing long-tail OOMs and exacerbating fragmentation.
investigative_steps: Collected GPU allocator histograms and slab metadata from impacted nodes.
Injected artificial heartbeat pauses in staging to reproduce allocation map drift.
Instrumented eviction queue with epoch counters and cross-validated with session lifecycle events.
Ran binary search on commits touching eviction and allocator code paths from last six months to rule out recent regressions.
Validated reproduction against both Hosted multi-tenant and Dedicated single-tenant images to confirm cross-env trigger.
fix_description: Introduce an epoched eviction/allocator handshake: eviction work is annotated with an epoch token that allocator honours when applying bitmap mutations. Bitmap writes now include a short-lived guard token preventing out-of-order application during concurrent session tear-downs. Add immediate compaction hook triggered when a node observes >X orphaned slabs and a fast-path reclaim invoked during eviction completion. Also add backpressure on eviction queue to keep processing latency within SLO bounds.
testing_notes: Unit tests: added deterministic eviction/allocator interleaving fuzz tests to cover epoch edge cases.
Integration: staging harness ran 48-hour churn with heartbeat delays injected; no orphaned slabs observed in 20 runs.
Performance: microbenchmarks show <2% avg CPU overhead and negligible median latency impact; tail latency improved under contention due to reduced full-compaction frequency.
Canary: deployed to 5% Hosted and 1 Dedicated pool for 72 hours; GPU OOM alerts suppressed and memory fragmentation metrics stabilized.
rollout_plan: Phase A (canary): runtime-1.30+hotfix on 5% Hosted, 1 Dedicated pool. Monitor orphaned_slab_count, gpu_oom_rate, eviction_latency every 5m.
Phase B (gradual): expand to 25% Hosted + 3 Dedicated pools after 48h clean canary window.
Phase C (full): global rollout to Hosted + Dedicated + Private air-gapped bundles after automated upgrade verification and security sign-off.
Fallback: automatic rollback if gpu_oom_rate increases by >10% relative to baseline or orphaned_slab_count increases for 3 consecutive windows.
rollback_plan: Rollback to runtime-1.29 image for canary nodes via standard deployment pipeline; if Dedicated customer requires immediate remediation, coordinate node reboot + manual compaction script and escalate to on-call infra for data-plane assistance.
notes: Design trade-offs considered: tighter allocator locking would be simpler but risked latency regression; chosen epoched approach aims to preserve allocator fast-path while providing correctness. We will follow-up with a refactor to expose allocator metrics to tenant-level dashboards and drive smarter autoscaling policies.
communication: 2026-02-20 - Customer TLs notified about active investigation and short-term mitigation steps (graceful node restarts).
2026-02-25 - Customer post-update emails with canary results and expected timeline for full rollout.
2026-03-06 - Plan to publish a short postmortem and mitigation cookbook for Dedicated customers.
